title: Java News Roundup: JDK 28 Schedule, Oracle CPUs, eMudhra Certs, Apache POI, WildFly, Azul, BellSoft
gist: InfoQ's Java roundup for the week of October 19, 2026 covers Oracle's October CPU, a proposed JDK 28 schedule with GA on March 9, 2027, and the eMudhra intermediate CA key compromise, which Azul says is especially dangerous for Java because it does not check revocation by default.

themes.theme: eMudhra CA compromise and Java exposure

insights.claim: Mozilla disclosed that eight private keys of eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were compromised, meaning an attacker holding any of them could impersonate any website or service.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: A CA-key compromise undermines TLS trust broadly and forces coordinated trust-store blocking.

insights.claim: The compromised certificates were blocked in Firefox and Chrome from October 17, on Microsoft platforms from October 20 and on Apple products from October 22, with responsible disclosure to downstream trust stores on October 19.
insights.speaker: Mozilla
insights.so_what: Staggered protection windows across vendors left gaps measured in days.
insights.quote: The certificates have been blocked in Firefox and Chrome since the 17th of October, on Microsoft platforms since the 20th and on Apple products since the 22nd.
insights.locator: The root programs and many downstream trust stores

insights.claim: Java does not check certificate revocation by default, so until the certificates are blocked in the JDK itself a Java application accepts a fraudulent certificate issued with those keys as valid, and no quarterly release was due until January.
insights.speaker: Azul
insights.so_what: Java estates were uniquely exposed and depend on out-of-cycle vendor patches for trust-store fixes.
insights.quote: Java makes this worse than it sounds: it does not check certificate revocation by default.
insights.locator: Java makes this worse than it sounds

insights.claim: The breach surfaced one day after Oracle's October CPU, a zero-day no quarterly schedule could have planned for, and Azul shipped an out-of-cycle update on October 21.
insights.speaker: Azul
insights.so_what: Quarterly patch cadences are inadequate for supply-chain and PKI incidents, favoring vendors that ship out-of-cycle fixes.
insights.locator: Within a day it was not enough anymore

insights.claim: Oracle's October 2026 Critical Patch Update shipped JDK versions 27.0.1, 25.0.5, 21.0.13, 17.0.21, 11.0.33 and 8u511.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Shows the active LTS set (8, 11, 17, 21, 25) that enterprises still need patched.

insights.claim: Mark Reinhold proposed a JDK 28 schedule (the text says JDK 24) with Rampdown Phase One on December 3, 2026, initial release candidate on February 4, 2027 and general availability on March 9, 2027, with review concluding October 29, 2026.
insights.speaker: Mark Reinhold
insights.so_what: Sets the planning date for the next feature release in March 2027.

insights.claim: Azul's October 2026 CPU covers 53 CVEs across Zulu versions 27, 25, 21, 17, 11, 8, 7 and 6, including an out-of-cycle update for the eMudhra certificates.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Third-party OpenJDK distributors are supporting very old versions, a niche commercial support market.
insights.locator: Concurrent with Oracle's Critical Patch Update

insights.claim: BellSoft's Liberica releases note 1438 overall fixes and backports in which BellSoft participated in eliminating 144 issues across all releases.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Indicates the share of upstream fixes contributed by downstream vendors, roughly 10%.
insights.locator: With an overall total of 1438 fixes

insights.claim: WildFly 42 adds virtual-thread support in its Jakarta Concurrency implementation and Apache POI 6.0.0 requires a minimum of JDK 17 and now uses cached values for formula cells by default.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Libraries are raising the Java baseline and adopting virtual threads, pushing enterprise upgrades.

insights.claim: Micronaut 5.2.3 resolves 10 CVEs in Micronaut Core 5.2.17 and Micronaut Security 5.4.1, and Open Liberty 26.0.0.11 beta adds workload identity in JWT builder plus a Netty-based HTTP transport preview.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Routine maintenance signals continued security churn in Java frameworks.
